Now, I don’t know how you steal a record slowly. I mean, maybe in a wahoo sort of fashion, but certainly not casually put it up your shirt or something. Just physically doesn’t work.

As of this post, Capture One does not support export to either AVIF or JPEG XL, image formats that offer better compression than JPEG and WebP, support greater color bit-depth, and are now widely supported in browsers [ AVIF , JPEG XL at caniuse.com ]. This being the case, the process I’ve settled on for generating AVIFs for new photos I post here is as follows.

Export 16-bit TIFF files from Capture One to a temporary folder.

Set up a GraphicConverter File menu > Auto Convert rule to watch the temporary folder and convert files that appear in it to AVIF. A quality setting around 50 seems like a good balance and 10- or 12-bit color depth ensures that most of the colors you see in the TIFF are retained. Unless you want to keep the (relatively massive) TIFF files around, set the rule to delete files once they are processed. GraphicConverter has to be open for Auto Convert to run.

The novel, genetically attenuated whole parasite PfSPZ-LARC2 Vaccine for malaria achieved an 87% efficacy rate in preventing infection during a recent phase 1 trial.

Among 22 participants exposed to a controlled malaria challenge 12 to 16 weeks after their last dose of vaccine, all seven placebo recipients became infected while only two of 15 vaccinated individuals developed an infection. All infected participants were safely and promptly treated. In addition, the vaccine was safe and well tolerated in the vaccinated participants.

These breakthrough findings were presented today at the annual meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene (External link) near Washington, D.C. They were reported by Dr. Sean C. items.title: Do nothing
items.label: Blogs
items.excerpt:
An exercise, a challenge.

Have a notebook ready.

Set an alarm for five minutes.

Relax.

Stare at a wall.

And do nothing.

Just wait for the alarm to sound.

But do not anticipate.

Let your mind wander.

When the timer goes off, fill the notebook with your thoughts.

Do not overthink.

Do not process.

Just write whatever.

Words, phrases.

Fragments.

St. Kateri Tekakwitha 😇

Humble & down-to earth Kateri (c. 1656 – April 17, 1680) — known as the Lily of the Mohawks, Mystic of the Wilderness, Healer of the New World, and the Mohawk Maiden — was a 17th-century Mohawk-Algonquin woman baptized around age 20 by Jesuit missionaries on Easter Sunday, 1676, taking the name Catherine (Kateri in Mohawk).

She was born in 1656 in the Mohawk village of Ossernenon, near what is now Auriesville, to a Mohawk father and an Algonquin Christian mother.  The Mohawk people traditionally had three major clans: Turtle, Bear, and Wolf.  Kateri was connected to the Turtle 🐢 Clan.  Smallpox killed her parents and brother when she was about four, leaving her with a scarred face and poor eyesight.  Her uncle raised her.

Her refusal to marry and her devotion to her new faith (such as observing Sunday as a holy day) drew hostility and threats from members of her community.  In 1677, she traveled roughly 200 miles north to the Christian Indigenous settlement…

items.title: Building California School Trends
items.label: Small Web
items.excerpt:
We're trying to buy a house in one of the highest cost of living areas of the United States, and the schools aren't even good.

One thing we'd hear was "wealthier people are moving in who care about education, so this lower-performing school will improve". But was that true? How could we figure that out?

I ended up building California School Trends to solve for the problem.

Certain websites like Great Schools or Niche will show you their custom score, but it usually obfuscates the underlying fundamentals. Certain schools end up with a 7/10 that have top-decile test scores. Other schools with pretty mediocre test scores had a 9/10. Why? It was hard to tell. Were they trending up? Down? It was difficult to find out.

I ended up finding Page Turner, a non-profit that focuses on k-2nd grade reading proficiency. They had some pretty great stats, but only for reading proficiency, and it was a bit challenging to navigate their website.

items.title: Sharing KMS Keys and Secrets Across AWS Accounts - Who Can Still Stop, Delete, Rotate, and Audit Them | hidekazu-konishi.com
items.label: Small Web
items.excerpt: A design guide to who holds stop, delete, rotate, and audit after you hand an AWS KMS key or an AWS Secrets Manager secret to another account through four routes: a key policy statement, an AWS RAM resource share (added on 2026-11-16), a secret resource policy, and a cross-account replica (added on 2026-11-13). It covers how the default and AWS_RAM key policies are evaluated together, the grants that stay in effect after sharing stops, what disabling or scheduling deletion of a shared key leaves behind, and what a replica copies, rejects, and keeps after replication stops. items.title: Claude Code Channels - Pushing Events into a Running Session, Sender Allowlists, and Permission Relay | hidekazu-konishi.com
items.label: Small Web
items.excerpt: A channel server listed in .mcp.json cannot push anything into a Claude Code session until it passes two more gates: --channels for the session and the organization's channelsEnabled. This guide reads the research preview pages to show who can put text in front of Claude and who can approve its tools: the sender allowlist lives in the channel server and should key on the sender, not the room; with permission relay, anyone who can reply through the channel can allow or deny a tool call, the first answer wins, and the verdict covers that call only. It also counts nine paths where events or verdicts fail without an error. Checked on 2026-11-22.

Hello friends! Ladybird is now in alpha. You can download it for macOS and Linux.

I’ve been looking forward to writing this post for a long time. :^)

Ladybird is a browser with a new engine. The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork. The browser around it is modest, but functional.

This is an alpha, so some websites won’t work, and it will crash sometimes. When that happens, tell us! You can report a broken site from inside the browser. After a crash, you can read the crash report and decide whether to send it. Our privacy policy has the details.

We want security nerds to hack it! A new browser gets hacked, over and over, and that’s part of the process, so we make no promises about security today. When you pwn us, please tell us how so we can harden Ladybird!

My first proper article is Runtime Quality Requires Humans which is about the limitations of trying to use AI coding with complex systems. I built a new site because I was tired of dealing with ads and paywalls on sites like Medium.

This was also an experiment in using the Astro web framework to make a complex static site, which worked out really well. I wrote all of the article myself but around half of the website tech was written by Claude Code, which I talk about on the About page. If anyone has feedback or a question, I'd love to hear it here!

items.title: Feed the Scorchpot [$14.99] [Strategy] [Windows] [macOS]
items.label: Gaming
items.excerpt:
You struck a deal with a dragon: twenty years of protection for twenty years of dinner service. The island thrives under the beast's watchful eye, as long as the meals keep coming.

Every year, the dragon wakes up hungrier. You roll dice to work your island, harvest ingredients, fuse them into recipes, and cook them down in the Scorchpot — the pot you keep full or end up in. Get the meal right and you prosper. Get it wrong and you're smoke.

Build farmsteads, shrines, and harbors across your hex-grid island, each one changing how the board pays out. The best runs start with a handful of tiles and end with a machine that buries the dragon in food. Then the odds tighten, the dragon turns picky, and you tear the whole thing down and rebuild while it's on fire.

Feed the Scorchpot, keep the dragon happy, and outlast the contract.

Cook cleverly, plan badly, or just roll with it — the dragon doesn't care how you win, only that you feed the beast on time. And yes, you can pet the…

items.title: Juice Galaxy (formerly Juice World) [$5.00] [Role Playing] [Windows] [macOS] [Linux]
items.label: Gaming
items.excerpt:
Juice is everything. There is nothing in the Fog. There is no greater honor than to serve the Juice Queen, and the sky is definitely not made of plywood.

Juice Galaxy is a happy place to fly around and smack things and drink juice. And explore things. And just, flip around doing stuff. Use any of a multitude of weapons to clobber and devour the local wildlife. Gather juice to increase your power and take on more powerful enemies.The game is still in active development. There's still a ton of work to do. I want to polish the physics and add a ton more abilities, places, music, items, monsters, and story.Enjoy, and please feel free to leave feedback or suggestions.
